ranked_facts.why: ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF, and PR-segment elevation in lead aVR are characteristic of pericarditis
elevated troponin levels can be seen in both pericarditis and myocarditis

elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein are indicative of an inflammatory process, which is consistent with pericarditis, myopericarditis, and myocarditis, but not pulmonary embolism

a normal cardiac examination is more consistent with pericarditis and myopericarditis, which may not have significant cardiac dysfunction, whereas myocarditis and pulmonary embolism may have abnormal cardiac findings
